title: Preservation for an affine base, modulo the open-complement condition
statement:
Fix the purity coefficient conventions [def-pur-conventions], in particular $k=\overline{\mathbf F}_q$, $\ell\ne\operatorname{char}k$, $n\geq1$ and $A=A_{E,n}$. Let $X,Y$ be finite-type $k$-schemes and let $f:X\to Y$ be a separated finite-type $k$-morphism [def-weil-scheme-morphism-properties]. Use the constructible exceptional inverse image $Rf^!$ of [def-weil-exceptional-inverse-image], defined by transport of the ordinary etale exceptional adjoint; no right adjoint on the unrestricted ordinary pro-etale derived category is assumed.

Choose a finite affine open cover $\{V\}$ of $Y$, a finite affine open cover $\{U\}$ of each $f^{-1}(V)$, and closed immersions $i_U:U\hookrightarrow T_U=\mathbf A^{d_U}_V$, with $d_U\geq0$, such that the induced map $U\to V$ is $\pi_U i_U$, where the projection is $\pi_U:T_U\to V$ [def-sbc-affine-space]. Write $W_U=T_U\setminus i_U(U)$. Suppose that $(W_U,T_U)$ satisfies the etale open-complement condition at $A$ with a nonnegative integer constant $c_U$ [def-exc-open-complement-bound] for every chart. For a nonempty family of charts put
$$
 D=\max_U d_U,\qquad c=\max_U\bigl(c_U+1+2(D-d_U)\bigr).
$$
If the chart family is empty (so $X=\varnothing$), put $D=c=0$.

Then the two preservation conclusions are:

1. For all integers $a\leq b$,
$$
 L\in D_c^{[a,b]}(Y,A)\quad\Longrightarrow\quad
 Rf^!L\in D_c^{[a-2D,b-2D+c]}(X,A),
$$
where constructible intervals are as in [def-weil-constructible-intervals].
2. For all integers $a\leq b$, if $K\in D^b_{ctf}(Y,A)$ has Tor amplitude in $[a,b]$, then $Rf^!K$ is bounded constructible with Tor amplitude in $[a-2D,b-2D+c]$, in the sense of [def-weil-finite-tor-amplitude]. In particular $Rf^!$ carries $D^b_{ctf}(Y,A)$ into $D^b_{ctf}(X,A)$.

proof.text:
All exceptional functors in this argument are the transported etale adjoints, not unrestricted pro-etale adjoints. All these finite-type $k$-schemes are Noetherian by [lem-weil-pbc-finite-type-over-noetherian], applied to the spectrum of the field $k$; they are quasi-separated by [lem-weil-pbc-locally-noetherian-quasi-separated]. (A field is Noetherian because its only ideals are $0$ and the unit ideal.) A separated finite-type morphism between the finite-type $k$-schemes in the argument has a compactification by [thm-nagata-compactification]; its proper factor is finite type over $k$ and has finite dimension by [lem-kun-dimension-finite-type]. Thus [thm-sf-ambient-adjoint-class](2) supplies the adjunction on bounded-below objects of etale origin, with the canonical comparisons of its clause (3), as summarized in [cor-sf-ambient-adjoint-discharge]. By [lem-sf-proetale-constructible-origin](ii), bounded constructible inputs have etale-origin witnesses. The formula in [def-weil-exceptional-inverse-image] identifies the functor on such an input $
u_Y^*G$ with $
u_X^*f^	imes G$. Only this construction and the bounded-below adjunction are used at this stage; preservation of bounded constructibility is proved below. More explicitly, work in the categories $\mathcal C(T)=\mathcal D^+_{\mathrm{et}}(T,A)$ of complexes with an etale-origin witness [def-sf-etale-origin-subcategory]. The comparison [lem-sf-class-compact-support-comparison] gives $Rf_!
u_X^*G\cong
u_Y^*(Rf_!^{\mathrm{et}}G)$, so compact support preserves these categories. The transported right functor also takes values in them: its witness is $f^	imes R
u_{Y,*}L$, bounded below by the construction above. Thus the displayed Hom bijection restricts to an actual adjunction $\mathcal C(X)ightleftarrows\mathcal C(Y)$, before any constructible-preservation assertion is used.

source.place: Imported proof, availability of the right adjoints and Step 1; unit proof (iv), first sentence

proof.text:
For an affine base open $g:V\hookrightarrow Y$, put $X_V=f^{-1}(V)$, $h:X_V\hookrightarrow X$, and $f_V:X_V\to V$. The class-restricted clause of [cor-exc-base-change-open-immersion-general] gives the correctly typed isomorphism
$$
 Lh^*Rf^!L\cong Rf_V^!Lg^*L.
$$
Here both sides are objects on $X_V$. By [prop-exc-open-adjoint], the exceptional adjoint for $g$ is $Lg^*$; hence [thm-exc-explicit-preservation] for $g$ shows that $Lg^*L$ has the same constructible interval as $L$, and that $Lg^*K$ has the same Tor interval as $K$. The comparison is used only on bounded constructible inputs, exactly the unconditional class specified by the cited base-change statement.

source.place: Imported proof, Step 3 (base-open comparison), with the missing source restriction restored

proof.text:
Fix one chart and let $u':U\hookrightarrow X_V$, $u=hu':U\hookrightarrow X$. Write $d=d_U$, $T=T_U$, $i=i_U$, and $\pi=\pi_U$, so $f_Vu'=\pi i$. Open restriction preserves the categories $\mathcal C$ of Step 1: the inclusion defining the comparison morphism [def-weil-pbc-site-comparison-morphism], restricted to objects over $U$, is the inclusion for $U$ itself; hence $L(u')^*\nu_{X_V}^*G\cong\nu_U^*(G|_U)$, with witness $G|_U$. By [prop-exc-open-adjoint], the restriction of $L(u')^*$ is right adjoint to $R(u')_!$ on these categories.

For $M\in\mathcal C(U)$ and $N\in\mathcal C(V)$, Step 1 and [thm-sf-comp-composition] give the natural bijections
$$
\begin{aligned}
\operatorname{Hom}(M,Ri^!R\pi^!N)
&\cong\operatorname{Hom}(Ri_!M,R\pi^!N)\\
&\cong\operatorname{Hom}(R\pi_!Ri_!M,N)\\
&\cong\operatorname{Hom}(R(\pi i)_!M,N),\\
\operatorname{Hom}(M,L(u')^*Rf_V^!N)
&\cong\operatorname{Hom}(R(u')_!M,Rf_V^!N)\\
&\cong\operatorname{Hom}(Rf_{V,!}R(u')_!M,N)\\
&\cong\operatorname{Hom}(R(f_Vu')_!M,N).
\end{aligned}
$$
Since $f_Vu'=\pi i$, [lem-cat-right-adjoint-composition] identifies both right adjoints with $R(f_Vu')^!$ and gives
$$
L(u')^*Rf_V^!\cong R(f_Vu')^!\cong Ri^!R\pi^!.
$$
Consequently, for $N=Lg^*L$, Step 2 and composition of open restrictions give
$$
Lu^*Rf^!L\cong Ri^!R\pi^!N.
$$
All Hom calculations take place on the bounded-below etale-origin categories, where both compact support and its right adjoint are defined by Step 1; none assumes the preservation being proved.

source.place: Imported proof, Step 1; unit proof (iv), composition of the chart right adjoints

proof.text:
The affine-space projection $\pi:T\to V$ is smooth of pure relative dimension $d$ by [sbc-lem-affine-space-smooth]; over the affine $V=\operatorname{Spec}R$ it is separated, since its diagonal is defined in $\operatorname{Spec}R[x_1,\ldots,x_d,y_1,\ldots,y_d]$ by the equations $x_j-y_j=0$. Apply [cor-pur-smooth-admissibility] to obtain
$$
 B=R\pi^!N\in D_c^{[a-2d,b-2d]}(T,A)
$$
when $N\in D_c^{[a,b]}(V,A)$. If instead $N$ is bounded constructible with Tor amplitude $[a,b]$, the same corollary gives that $B$ is bounded constructible with Tor amplitude $[a-2d,b-2d]$. These are separate applications: the cohomological-interval assertion is not restricted to finite-Tor inputs.

source.place: Imported proof, Step 2, smooth projection; unit proof (iii) used in (iv)

proof.text:
To apply the closed-immersion bounds, pass explicitly to the etale site. By [lem-sf-proetale-constructible-origin](ii) choose $B'\in D^b_c(T_{\mathrm{et}},A)$ with $B\cong\nu_T^*B'$. Exactness and the cohomology formula of [lem-sf-comparison-pullback-exact], together with full faithfulness in [thm-weil-pbc-site-comparison], show that $B'$ has the same cohomological interval as $B$: a cohomology sheaf with zero comparison pullback is zero because that pullback is faithful. For the Tor application, [lem-sf-comparison-tor-amplitude](ii) gives the same Tor interval for $B'$. The defining transport formula [def-weil-exceptional-inverse-image], using the unit isomorphism of [thm-weil-pbc-site-comparison], identifies
$$
 Ri^!B\cong\nu_U^*i_{\mathrm{et}}^!B'.
$$
Thus the following closed-immersion calculation concerns ordinary etale adjoints and the etale complement condition, on the same coefficient ring $A$.

source.place: Imported proof, Step 2, site distinction needed before the closed-support computations; Stacks Tags 09AK and 04JC

proof.text:
By [def-exc-open-complement-bound], the assumed constant $c_U$ gives both $R^qj_*M=0$ for all etale $A$-module sheaves $M$ and $q>c_U$, and constructibility of every $R^qj_*F$ for constructible $F$, where $j:W_U\hookrightarrow T$. The ordinary etale closed adjoint is supplied by [lem-exc-closed-ambient]. Apply the constructible clause of [lem-exc-closed-amplitude] to $B'$ in the cohomological-interval application. In the Tor application apply [prop-exc-closed-tor] to the bounded constructible $B'$ of Step 5. The open $j$ is quasi-compact as required by the assumed open-complement condition. The resulting interval in either application is
$$
 [a-2d,b-2d+c_U+1].
$$
In both cases the result is bounded constructible. Pullback by $\nu_U^*$ preserves this constructibility by [lem-sf-proetale-constructible-origin](ii), and preserves its cohomological interval by [lem-sf-comparison-pullback-exact]. In the Tor application it preserves the Tor interval by [lem-sf-comparison-tor-amplitude](i). Combining with Steps 2–5 gives the claimed chartwise bounds for $Lu^*Rf^!$.

source.place: Imported proof, Step 2, closed-support calculation; unit proof (ii) used in (iv)

proof.text: Suppose the chart family is nonempty and put $I=[a-2D,b-2D+c]$. For each chart $d_U\leq D$, so $a-2D\leq a-2d_U$. Also $c\geq c_U+1+2(D-d_U)$ gives $b-2d_U+c_U+1\leq b-2D+c$. Hence every chartwise interval of Step 6 is contained in $I$. Vanishing outside a smaller interval implies vanishing outside $I$, for ordinary cohomology and for every tensor test defining Tor amplitude. If there are no charts, $X$ is empty; sheaves on its small pro-etale site are zero by the sheaf condition for the empty covering, so both conclusions hold with $D=c=0$.

source.place: Imported proof, Step 2, maximum of the chart bounds; empty-cover edge case made explicit

proof.text: Let $F=Rf^!L$ in the cohomological-interval application. Open restriction on constant-$A$ pro-etale module sheaves is exact by [prop-weil-pbc-proetale-constant-exact], so $\mathcal H^r(F)|_U=\mathcal H^r(F|_U)$: apply restriction to the kernel/image quotient defining cohomology. The latter vanishes for $r\notin I$ by Step 7. A sheaf zero on every $U$ is zero, since for any site object $P\to X$ its inverse images $P\times_XU$ cover it and every section restricting to zero is zero by the sheaf axiom. For $r\in I$, glue the finite constructible stratifications of the finitely many $\mathcal H^r(F)|_{U_i}$ as follows. Order the opens and replace the strata in $U_i$ by their intersections with $U_i\setminus\bigcup_{j<i}U_j$. These are finitely many locally closed constructible strata in $X$ (the opens here are quasi-compact, and the displayed difference is closed in $U_i$); they partition $X$. Pulling each local constant trivialization back to an intersection gives a local constant trivialization there with the same finite module, so the restrictions remain locally constant with finite stalks. This is precisely [def-weil-finite-torsion-constructibility]. Thus $F\in D_c^I(X,A)$ by [def-weil-constructible-intervals]. For any bounded constructible $K$, choose integers $a_0\leq b_0$ containing its finitely many nonzero cohomology degrees (choose $a_0=b_0=0$ when $K=0$). The first conclusion just proved, applied with $[a_0,b_0]$, gives bounded constructibility of $Rf^!K$.

source.place: Imported proof, Step 4; finite disjointification supplies the constructibility gluing argument

proof.text:
Finally let $K\in D^b_{ctf}(Y,A)$ have Tor amplitude $[a,b]$, and put $F=Rf^!K$, which is bounded constructible by Step 8. For an arbitrary pro-etale $A$-module sheaf $M$ on $X$, the ambient finite-level tensor comparison of [lem-pur-derived-pullback-tensor-iso] gives
$$
 Lu^*(F\otimes_A^LM)\cong Lu^*F\otimes_A^L u^*M.
$$
The use of a sheaf $u^*M$ in degree zero is justified by [prop-weil-pbc-proetale-constant-exact]. The right side has no cohomology outside $I$ by the chartwise Tor bound of Steps 6–7. Exact restriction commutes with the kernel/image quotient defining cohomology. For $r\notin I$, every section of $\mathcal H^r(F\otimes_A^LM)$ over a site object $P\to X$ restricts to zero on all $P\times_XU$; these form a covering, so the sheaf axiom makes the section zero. Hence $\mathcal H^r(F\otimes_A^LM)=0$ for $r\notin I$. This is the Tor-amplitude condition of [def-weil-finite-tor-amplitude] for every $M$, including sheaves not of etale origin. Bounded constructibility of $F$ and this finite interval prove the second assertion and the stated $D^b_{ctf}$ preservation.

blueprint_update.statement:
In the purity conventions of this chapter ([def-pur-conventions] fixed setting),
let $f:X\to Y$ be a
separated finite-type
morphism. The ambient exceptional right adjoint datum of
[def-weil-ambient-exceptional-adjoint] is not assumed: the right adjoints
$Rf^{\times}$, $R(\pi_U)^{\times}$, $R(i_U)^{\times}$ that the proof forms
exist on the bounded constructible and finite-Tor coefficients of the two
clauses below by [cor-sf-ambient-adjoint-discharge]. Cover $Y$ by finitely
many affine opens $V\subseteq Y$; for each $V$, $f^{-1}(V)$ is
covered by finitely many affine opens $U\subseteq f^{-1}(V)$, and each
$U\to V$ is affine of finite type, hence a closed subscheme of
$\mathbf A^{d_U}_V$ for some $d_U\in\mathbf Z_{\geq0}$, with open
complement $W_U=\mathbf A^{d_U}_V\setminus U$ in the
[def-sbc-affine-space] affine space. Assume the open-complement
condition of [def-exc-open-complement-bound] for every pair
$(W_U,\mathbf A^{d_U}_V)$ over the finitely many charts, with constants
$c_U$, and put $D=\max_U d_U$ and
$c=\max_U\bigl(c_U+1+2(D-d_U)\bigr)$. Then $f$
satisfies the two preservation clauses of
[def-weil-exceptional-adjoint-admissibility]:

1. for all integers $a\leq b$,
$$
L\in D_c^{[a,b]}(Y,A)\quad\Longrightarrow\quad
Rf^!L\in D_c^{[a-2D,b-2D+c]}(X,A);
$$
1. if $K\in D^b_{ctf}(Y,A)$ has
finite Tor amplitude in
$[a,b]$, then $Rf^!K$ has finite Tor amplitude in
$[a-2D,b-2D+c]$; in particular $Rf^!$ carries
$D^b_{ctf}(Y,A)$ into $D^b_{ctf}(X,A)$.

proof.text:
On a chart $U\subseteq f^{-1}(V)$ with $V$ affine the morphism
$U\to V$ is affine of finite type, so the presentation of its
coordinate ring as a quotient of a polynomial algebra over
$\mathcal O_V(V)$ exhibits it as a closed subscheme
$i_U:U\hookrightarrow\mathbf A^{d_U}_V$ ([def-sbc-affine-space]);
write $\pi_U:\mathbf A^{d_U}_V\to V$ for the projection and
$u_U:U\hookrightarrow X$ for the open immersion (an open immersion, since
$U\subseteq f^{-1}(V)\subseteq X$), so that $fu_U=\pi_Ui_U$.
Step 1: the right adjoint of the chart. The compact-support direct image
of a composite is the composite of the compact-support direct images, and
the right adjoint of a composite of functors is the composite of their
right adjoints, so

$$
R(fu_U)^{\times}\;\cong\;R(i_U)^{\times}\circ R(\pi_U)^{\times},
\qquad
Lu_U^*\circ Rf^{\times}\;\cong\;R(fu_U)^{\times},
$$

the second because $R(u_U)_!=u_{U!}$ has right adjoint $Lu_U^*$ by
[prop-exc-open-adjoint]. Hence it suffices to bound
$R(i_U)^{\times}R(\pi_U)^{\times}$.
Step 2: the chartwise bounds. Fix $V$ and a chart $U\subseteq f^{-1}(V)$, and write $d=d_U$, $c'=c_U$. The projection $\pi_U$ is
smooth of pure relative dimension $d$, so
[cor-pur-smooth-admissibility] gives, for
$L\in D_c^{[a,b]}(V,A)$,

$$
R(\pi_U)^{\times}L\in D_c^{[a-2d,b-2d]}(\mathbf A^{d}_V,A),
$$

and for $K$ with finite Tor amplitude in $[a,b]$, finite Tor amplitude
in $[a-2d,b-2d]$; the closed immersion $i_U$ has ambient right
adjoint $R(i_U)^{\times}$ by [lem-exc-closed-ambient], and the
closed-support computations [lem-exc-closed-amplitude] and
[prop-exc-closed-tor], applied to the pair $(i_U,W_U)$ under the
assumed open-complement condition, move the interval to
$[a-2d,b-2d+c'+1]$. The exact restriction $Lu_U^*$ preserves both
kinds of bound ([thm-exc-explicit-preservation] for the open immersion $u_U$), so each chart carries the interval
$[a-2d_U,b-2d_U+c_U+1]$, which is contained in
$[a-2D,b-2D+c]$ by the choice of $D$ and $c$.
Step 3: passage from the affine opens of the base to the base. For an
affine open $V\subseteq Y$ with open immersion $g_V:V\hookrightarrow Y$
and $f_V:f^{-1}(V)\to V$, the base-change comparison for the open
immersion $g_V$ is an isomorphism by
[cor-exc-base-change-open-immersion-general], i.e.
$Rf_V^{\times}\cong Lg_V^*\circ Rf^{\times}$; that statement is read on the
coefficients of the present theorem, where the ambient datum it displays as a
hypothesis is the theorem [cor-sf-ambient-adjoint-discharge], so that
the comparison used here is unconditional, and both sides are applied only to
the bounded constructible complexes $Lg_V^*K$ with
$K\in D_c^{[a,b]}(Y,A)$. Applying Step 2 to the
separated finite-type morphism $f_V$ over the affine scheme $V$
therefore bounds $Lg_V^*(Rf^{\times}K)\cong Rf_V^{\times}(Lg_V^*K)$ on
$f^{-1}(V)$, hence on each chart $U\subseteq f^{-1}(V)$.
Step 4: conclusion. Vanishing of a cohomology sheaf, and vanishing of the
cohomology of a complex tensored with a coefficient sheaf, are local on the
site, and the charts $U$ cover $X$; hence the chartwise bounds of
Steps 2–3 give the two displayed assertions for the global object
$Rf^{\times}K$.
